text.what: A Portuguese bakery on Kapahulu Avenue in Honolulu that made the malasada an everyday Hawaiian habit rather than a Carnival one.
text.story:
Margaret and Frank Leonard Rego Sr. opened the bakery in 1952. Rego's mother pushed him to sell malasadas — the holeless Portuguese pastry Portuguese immigrants had brought to the islands at the turn of the twentieth century. Leonard's carried it to a far wider audience than it had before.

A franchise location opened in Japan in 2008.
text.today: A household name in Hawaii and known well beyond it; the malasada wagons park across the island.
